title: Kernel sidecar field diary — jitter, compaction, and microbatch anomalies
content:
Quick overview:
This is a freeform field diary capturing the odd, small-ticket experiments and noisy incidents we saw over the last week while running the kernel-sidecar prototype in shadow on staging and two small production canaries. Primary focus: jitter when the sidecar is attached, KV cache compaction interactions, and unexpected microbatch splits under ~50ms tail latency pressure.

Attendees / who scribbled this down:
- Priya Menon (owner, writing)
- Carlos Rivera (ran the perf traces)
- Ava Chen (oncall, repro and rollback)
- Samir Patel (kernel-sidecar implementer)
- Jun Park (observability wiring)

High-level summary of what we observed:
- Attach jitter: ~0.5–2% of requests hitting nodes with sidecar saw initial token emission delay of 8–20ms vs baseline. Not consistent across models; more pronounced for short sequences (<16 tokens).
- Compaction thrash: aggressive KV compaction that runs after N cold fills caused temporary KV miss amplification (~1.6x requests to KVS) for ~4–7s while compaction swept slots.
- Microbatch split anomaly: under pressure when arrival variance spiked (sustained 2.2x lambda over 30s), the batcher split some 32→two 16 microbatches but failed to coalesce quickly; extra scheduling cost added ~6–12ms per request tail.

Experiment log (chronological):
1) 2029-05-01 (staging, shadow): attach sidecar with lightweight tracing enabled. Baseline saw jitter. Carlos pulled pprof + ftrace; root cause trace shows an extra sysclock syscall path triggered by sidecar heartbeat timer when prefill path had <8 tokens. Hypothesis: sidecar timer callback race with prefill path entry. Ticket created INF-4312.
2) 2029-05-03 (prod canary A): toggled compaction threshold from 30s idle to 90s. Observed reduction in KV miss amplification but still a short tail when compaction starts. Raised compaction to be cooperative instead of stop-the-world (ran a prototype patch).
3) 2029-05-05 (prod canary B): increased batch coalescing window from 2ms→4ms for short sequences. That reduced split frequency but introduced a slight median latency bump (~1.7ms).
4) 2029-05-06 (load test): synthetic high-variance arrival spikes reproduced microbatch split scenario; added coalescer fast-path in experiment branch; memory overhead within acceptable range.

Key data points (from traces / perf dashboards):
- Attach jitter incidence: 0.9% of requests across canary nodes (95th percentile extra delay 16ms).
- KV miss amplification during compaction: QPS to KVS increased by 1.6x for 4–7s windows; CPU on canary nodes spiked by 12% during those windows.
- Microbatch split added latency: median +1.8ms, p99 +12.3ms during spike windows.

Observations and quick hypotheses:
- Sidecar heartbeat code path does an STL map lookup guarded by a spinlock; under high interleaving the syscall to clock_gettime appears and forces a kernel transition that is higher cost on some EC2 instance types.
- Compaction currently does slot eviction in a single-threaded sweep; moving to chunked cooperative compaction should smooth the impact.
- Batcher heuristics rely on arrival variance sampling that is too slow to react to sudden lambda bursts; need an instantaneous jitter detector to avoid harmful splits.

Actions taken this week (short-term fixes):
- Rolled sidecar heartbeat timer from CLOCK_REALTIME to CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW on staging (Priya) — small improvement in jitter variance.
- Landed patch to make compaction chunked/cooperative in prototype branch (PR #1254) so compaction yields every 64 slots. Carlos validated no functional regressions.
- Temporarily increased coalescing window for short sequences on canary B; monitoring for downstream tail effects (Ava).
- Added an instantaneous variance metric (arrival_inst_var) to per-core telemetry so we can alarm earlier. Jun wired the metric to /alerts/prefill-coalescer.

Outstanding questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Is the clock syscall the real culprit or just correlated? Reproduce on bare metal dev box (Samir) where kernel noise is lower.
- Evaluate if moving spinlock to MCS lock reduces syscall occurrences. Cost/benefit? (PR experimental branch).
- Should compaction be policy-driven per-model? Heuristic: longer-context / high-traffic models tolerate aggressive compaction; short-chat workloads do not. Need dataset.
- Coalescer: add a fast-path that explicitly forbids splitting when instant variance > threshold AND tail SLO alarm is active. How do we tune threshold without regressing median?

Small runbook notes (for oncall):
- If p99 token emission jumps by >10ms for sidecar nodes, run: curl admin/sidecar/state -> check heartbeat timer drift -> flip sidecar-heartbeat-mode to "cooperative".
- If KVS QPS jumps and CPU spikes: temporarily scale compaction worker count to 0 (disable) -> monitor for memory pressure; escalate to infra if memory increases.

Decisions and temporary policies agreed in sync:
- Keep sidecar enabled on canary A but disable on any node with t2-family instances (we saw worse syscall overhead there).
- Treat compaction as cooperative by default in all staging/dev clusters until we verify long-tail memory stability.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Samir: run bare-metal reproducibility test and post traces to INF-4312 by 2029-05-11.
- Carlos: complete latency attribution slice for attach jitter and publish p99 breakdown in /dash/attach-jitter by 2029-05-12.
- Ava: monitor canary B for median regression and be ready to rollback coalescing window by 2029-05-10 23:59 UTC.
- Jun: add arrival_inst_var alarm thresholds and runbook doc snippet by 2029-05-09.
- Priya: prototype MCS lock patch and quick perf run (dev box) by 2029-05-14.

Misc notes and free-form fragments (copied from meeting):
- "we're seeing the sidecar behave like a thin syscall amplifier" — Carlos
- "compaction wants to be polite, but it's still hungry at 3am" — oncall banter
- question: do we want model-tagged compaction policies stored in plan-control plane? (product signal: maybe yes)

Meeting cadence / next sync:
- Quick follow-up sync Thursday 09:00 PT (15 minutes) — focused on Samir's bare-metal repro and Carlos's trace diff.
- Full weekly runtime ops retro next Tuesday 10:30 PT.
